question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the RFC’s core Claw lifecycle, including package-sourced managed workspace files and their persistent ownership ledger?
rationale: The implementation appears mechanically sound, but automation cannot decide whether this new core installation and trust model belongs in the product or whether the stacked lifecycle should continue.

options.title: Pause pending sponsorship
options.body: Keep the protected stack open but do not land further slices until an authorized maintainer explicitly accepts the RFC and trust boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the lifecycle
options.body: Approve the direction, require real isolated CLI proof, and review and land the dependent PRs in order.

options.title: Decline the core feature
options.body: Close the implementation stack if package-managed Claw lifecycle ownership is not planned for OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Pause pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the protected stack open but do not land further slices until an authorized maintainer explicitly accepts the RFC and trust boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history points to this person as the strongest owner for shared-state architecture and the core product decision.
